design_goal.primary: Preserve the Tiam1 PDZ fold and Caspr4 A-peptide canonical binding while weakening the Syndecan-1 B-peptide interface.
design_goal.formal_success_definition: A feasible candidate generated under an auditable whole-protein adaptive Dual-AST improves the same-protocol A-over-B structural-interface margin without losing the apo fold or the A complex. The outer LLM may create, delete, migrate, resize, or rewire nodes anywhere in the reviewed P chain, while deterministic safety activates only 4-8 positions per round.

positive_signals: A complex retains a canonical, clash-free PDZ-peptide pose.
A interface strength remains high while B interface strength decreases.
Apo PDZ confidence and the shared terminal-carboxylate anchor remain intact.
failure_signals: Any mutation outside the active compiled AST selector or inside a globally protected residue span.
A severe chain break, core/interface clash, or extremely low A-complex confidence.
Apparent selectivity produced by globally unfolding the PDZ domain or disrupting both peptide states.

mutable_residue_spans.role: whole-protein review envelope; this does not make every residue mutable at once because the active scope is selected by the safety-reviewed Executable Dual-AST

per_round_active_budget.policy: The LLM proposes scope and residue preferences; deterministic safety compilation is authoritative.

information_gaps: AF3, Protenix, and ESMFold confidence are not affinity oracles.
The experimental structure matrix lacks WT+A and engineered+B cross structures.
Any new sequence requires paired A/B Kd measurements and a folding/stability assay.
provisional_assumptions: All candidates are compared with the same structure protocol and seed policy.
The peptide sequences have free C termini even though the sequence-only input has no terminal modification token.
The closed-book search is evaluated against the known engineered reference only after ranking.
